items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: the style that Goodman introduced when he had the first Mandela and then Jaime Schertzer playing lead sax.

ctx.x: I thought I'd get off on a long ramping subject. And it came to me. We talked one time about what style it was, you know, like a man could be reading music, say reading lead saxophone part and give an entirely different sound of the section. Absolutely.

But you can see that today in say a band like Les Elgart. It's true that they have distinctive music in the arrangement but there is also a distinctive sound to the sax section as they follow the leader. A very distinctive sound, different from any other band. But there was much more of that in those days. For every band the section would have a distinctive sound. Sometimes in the brass it was harder to do this in the brass but Isham Jones' brass had a distinctive sound to it. And very often the sax because there…
But what do you think it is that makes for a style?
